description: Empirical reasoning schemas and archetypes for the diagnostic JavaScript and TypeScript baseline check; deeper language internals are carried by PRG-T01.

archetypes.name: Defensive Primitive Sanitization & Coercion Guard
archetypes.coreConcept: Distinguishing primitive types from reference values, enforcing strict equality, and handling nullish values (null/undefined) safely without overwriting legitimate falsy values (0, false, empty string).
mentalModel: 1. Identify whether incoming properties are primitive values (number, string, boolean) or missing (null, undefined).
2. Use strict equality (===) and nullish coalescing (??) instead of logical OR (||) to preserve legitimate 0 or false values.
3. Return sanitized data transfer object conforming to the schema specification.
archetypes.governingInvariant: sanitizedValue = (inputVal !== null && inputVal !== undefined) ? inputVal : defaultValue

cognitiveTraps.name: Falsy Zero Value Overwrite
cognitiveTraps.description: Using 'val || defaultVal' overwrites valid 0 or empty string with default values.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass { timeoutSec: 0 }; with || default of 30, it incorrectly yields 30 instead of 0.

cognitiveTraps.name: Loose Equality Implicit Coercion
cognitiveTraps.description: Comparing with '==' causes unintended coercion between false, 0, and empty strings.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Comparing '' == 0 returns true, bypassing empty string validation.

cognitiveTraps.name: Truthiness Conflating Valid Falsy Values
cognitiveTraps.description: Checking '!val' treats legitimate 0, false, or '' the same as null or undefined.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass port = 0 to hasValidPort; '!port' rejects 0 instead of distinguishing missing vs zero.

cognitiveTraps.name: Content Mistaken for Identity
cognitiveTraps.description: Two separately created structured values may contain the same fields yet still compare as different references.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A predicted comparison between two independently constructed but structurally equal records is marked equal; the runtime comparison is false.

cognitiveTraps.name: One Conversion Rule Assumed Everywhere
cognitiveTraps.description: Boolean tests, arithmetic, equality, and runtime classification can apply different language rules to the same value.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A trace checks an empty-like value in a conditional and then compares it numerically; one predicted result incorrectly reuses the other context’s conversion.

realWorldDomains.description: Sanitizing environment variable overrides for microservice configuration.
Normalizing user settings where 0 or false are valid operational thresholds.

qualityChecks.check: Missing-value guards and defaults distinguish `null`/`undefined` from legitimate falsy values (`0`, `false`, `''`) by structure rather than truthy/falsy coercion.
qualityChecks.why: Truthy/falsy coercion silently drops valid `0`, `false`, or `''` values on untested branches.

qualityChecks.check: Sanitization constructs an explicit output object with only the intended schema fields rather than forwarding unvalidated properties from the input.
qualityChecks.why: Spreading raw input objects leaks unexpected or unvalidated fields downstream.

qualityChecks.check: Defaulting and validation intent is explicit at the boundary rather than spread across implicit truthy/falsy expressions.
qualityChecks.why: Scattered coercion obscures which values the caller contract considers absent.

knownBad.code: function readLimit(config) { const raw = config.limit; return raw || 10; }

levelNotes.L1: Classify scalar and structured values and use types that match their roles.
levelNotes.L2: Predict identity and ordinary coercion outcomes from short expressions.
levelNotes.L3: Explain boundary behavior for absent values, unusual numbers, and built-in runtime categories.

archetypes.source: ECMAScript and TypeScript language semantics; cores: exercism-javascript, exercism-typescript, javascript-koans, javascript-questions, wtfjs

archetypes.name: Encapsulated Lexical Scope & Closure State Factory
archetypes.coreConcept: Creating private state enclosed within execution context boundaries, exposing controlled accessors without leaking internal data structures.
mentalModel: 1. Initialize private state variables inside the outer factory function frame.
2. Return an object interface whose methods form closures over the private state.
3. Ensure external mutation cannot compromise internal state references.
archetypes.governingInvariant: privateState accessible exclusively through returned accessor functions; outer lexical frame retained in heap

cognitiveTraps.name: Internal Reference Escape
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning a direct reference to an internal mutable array or object allows external mutation bypassing encapsulation.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Call state.getAll(); mutate returned array; internal registry is corrupted without calling add().

realWorldDomains.description: Thread-safe event counter tracking request latency buckets and hit counts.
In-memory token vault holding ephemeral credentials with controlled expiration.

qualityChecks.check: No reference to internal mutable state escapes the factory through any accessor or return value.
qualityChecks.why: Returning a live internal reference lets callers mutate private closure state outside the factory API.

qualityChecks.check: Mutable state lives in lexical bindings inside the factory closure rather than as properties on the returned object.
qualityChecks.why: Storing state on the returned object exposes it to direct external reassignment.

qualityChecks.check: The returned interface exposes only the intended domain operations, without leaking internal helpers or raw state setters.
qualityChecks.why: Exposing internal mutators breaks the factory's encapsulation boundary.

archetypes.name: Immutable Collection Transformation Pipeline
archetypes.coreConcept: Processing and summarizing datasets using pure transformation pipelines (map, filter, reduce) without mutating input collections.
mentalModel: 1. Filter input records by required business status or timestamp range.
2. Map/transform matching records into normalized reporting schemas.
3. Reduce into structured aggregations (grouping by key, summing totals, computing percentiles).

cognitiveTraps.name: In-Place Array Sort Mutation
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling Array.prototype.sort() directly on input array mutates the original order unexpectedly.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Call sortOrders(orders); check original orders array order; order was permanently altered.

cognitiveTraps.name: Reduce Without Initial Accumulator
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling reduce() without an explicit initial accumulator throws TypeError on empty arrays and reuses the first element.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Call sumTotals([]); without an initial value, reduce throws TypeError.

cognitiveTraps.name: Callback Effect Confused with Returned Result
cognitiveTraps.description: A callback side effect does not supply the transformed collection value, and selection, mapping, and aggregation have different result shapes.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A predicted pipeline contains no transformed entries because its callback only records a side effect; a focused output assertion catches the empty or malformed result.

cognitiveTraps.name: Transformation Loses Entry Alignment
cognitiveTraps.description: A collection transformation can produce plausible values while dropping, duplicating, or moving entries.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Tests compare output length and each output position with the corresponding input after mapping; a missing or reordered entry fails.

cognitiveTraps.name: Accumulator Starts or Advances Incorrectly
cognitiveTraps.description: An absent initial state changes the first callback input, while a faulty update can discard prior contributions.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Tests cover empty, one-entry, and several-entry inputs; the empty case exposes a missing seed and the larger case exposes a lost prior total.

cognitiveTraps.name: Mutation Effect Confused with Operation Result
cognitiveTraps.description: An operation may change a collection while returning a different value, and edits during traversal can change later visits.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A test separately inspects the collection after the operation, the returned value, and the visited-entry sequence.

realWorldDomains.description: Aggregating daily settlement revenue by category with tax breakdowns.
Summarizing microservice error counts grouped by HTTP response code.

qualityChecks.check: Transformation stages derive new collections without mutating caller-owned arrays or intermediate elements.
qualityChecks.why: In-place array methods such as `.sort()` or `.reverse()` corrupt the caller's ordering.

qualityChecks.check: Filtering, projection, and aggregation are structured as distinct, readable stages rather than a single monolithic loop or reducer mixing all three.
qualityChecks.why: Separating pipeline stages keeps each transformation easy to reason about, test, and extend.

qualityChecks.check: Aggregation has a focused stage with its initial state and update policy visible at one boundary.
qualityChecks.why: An opaque or mixed-purpose aggregation is difficult to review and extend safely.

knownBad.code: function summarize(rows) { let output = {}; for (const row of rows) { if (row.active) output[row.group] = (output[row.group] ?? 0) + row.amount; } return output; }

levelNotes.L1: Implement one-to-one transformations and selection with preserved order.
levelNotes.L2: Distinguish callback return contracts and establish correct accumulator behavior.
levelNotes.L3: Compose typed stages while preserving inputs, shape, and traversal expectations.

archetypes.source: ECMAScript and TypeScript language semantics; cores: eslint, exercism-javascript, javascript-koans, javascript-questions, typescript-exercises

archetypes.name: DOM Event Delegation & Propagation Controller
archetypes.coreConcept: Managing dynamic UI interactions via parent delegation, accounting for event bubbling from nested child elements (e.g. icons, spans inside buttons), and preventing event propagation issues.
mentalModel: 1. Attach a single listener to the container element rather than each child row.
2. On event trigger, traverse upward using event.target.closest(selector) to match the interactive boundary.
3. Ensure clicks on nested children (icons, bold tags) trigger the correct handler with the parent dataset attributes.
archetypes.governingInvariant: delegatedTarget = event.target.closest('[data-action]'); handler executed with target dataset attributes

cognitiveTraps.name: Direct Target Assumption on Nested Elements
cognitiveTraps.description: Inspecting event.target.dataset directly instead of event.target.closest('[data-action]') fails when clicking inner <span> or <i>.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Simulate click with event.target = <span> nested inside <button data-action='delete'>; target.dataset is empty.

cognitiveTraps.name: Null Dereference on Non-Matching Container Click
cognitiveTraps.description: Dereferencing the matched action element without guarding against null throws when clicking non-interactive background areas.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Click container padding outside any [data-action] element; handler throws TypeError.

realWorldDomains.description: Handling row action buttons (edit, delete, view) in high-throughput virtualized data tables.
Managing interactive task card interactions across dynamic columns.

qualityChecks.check: Delegated event handlers resolve the interactive boundary upward from `event.target` and guard against non-matching clicks before reading attributes.
qualityChecks.why: Reading `event.target` directly misses nested children (`<span>`, icons), and unguarded lookups crash on container clicks.

qualityChecks.check: DOM target lookup is separated from action execution so handlers do not couple DOM traversal to business state updates.
qualityChecks.why: Decoupling target resolution from action dispatch makes the business handler testable without DOM events.

archetypes.name: Resilient Async Microtask & Promise Combinator
archetypes.coreConcept: Orchestrating concurrent asynchronous operations with partial failure tolerance, microtask coordination, and deterministic timeout aborts.
mentalModel: 1. Accept an array of asynchronous tasks and execute them concurrently.
2. Isolate failures so that individual task rejections do not abort surviving tasks.
3. Return structured settlement results partitioned into fulfilled values and rejected errors.
archetypes.governingInvariant: results.length === tasks.length; all promises settled before resolving combinator

cognitiveTraps.name: Premature Fast-Fail with Promise.all
cognitiveTraps.description: Using Promise.all for independent tasks causes a single transient failure to abort all other valid results.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: 3 tasks run; task 2 fails; results of task 1 and 3 are lost.

cognitiveTraps.name: Completion-Order Result Array Drift
cognitiveTraps.description: Pushing resolved values into an array inside .then() reorders results by completion time instead of input order.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Task 0 takes 30ms, task 1 takes 5ms; output has task 1's result at index 0.

cognitiveTraps.name: Pending Work Mistaken for Its Result
cognitiveTraps.description: A completion handle represents work that may settle later; reading it as the fulfilled value skips the asynchronous boundary.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A predicted trace uses a pending completion object where a later consumer expects the fulfilled data; an awaited-result assertion exposes the mismatch.

cognitiveTraps.name: Started Work Not Connected to the Caller
cognitiveTraps.description: A callback can start asynchronous work yet omit returning it, hiding its outcome from downstream stages.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A regression check waits on the public operation and verifies both the final value and rejection; it completes too early or misses the inner failure when work is detached.

cognitiveTraps.name: Deferred Reaction Placed in the Synchronous Phase
cognitiveTraps.description: Promise reactions run after the current synchronous sequence, and later observations depend on settlement and chaining.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: An exact event-trace prediction puts a reaction before a synchronous marker; the expected sequence check fails.

cognitiveTraps.name: Completion Speed Mistaken for Output Position
cognitiveTraps.description: Concurrent tasks may finish in a different order from their inputs even when results remain associated with original positions.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Tests give tasks deliberately different completion times and compare each output with its originating input.

realWorldDomains.description: Aggregating upstream service dependency health checks with per-service latency.
Preloading critical UI assets in parallel with graceful fallbacks.

qualityChecks.check: When partial failure tolerance is required, each concurrent task's rejection is isolated so one failure does not abort or drop sibling results.
qualityChecks.why: Unisolated rejections discard valid results from concurrent sibling tasks.
accepted: per-task async wrapper with try/catch returning { status, value | reason }

qualityChecks.check: Every spawned promise is awaited or returned in the combinator's settlement chain, with no detached fire-and-forget async work.
qualityChecks.why: Unawaited async calls cause unhandled rejections and return before work completes.

qualityChecks.check: Asynchronous work is connected to its caller through a returned or awaited completion path, with independent work coordinated in a focused boundary.
qualityChecks.why: Detached tasks obscure ownership of completion and failure handling.

knownBad.code: async function refresh() { persistLater(); }

levelNotes.L1: Return and observe asynchronous completion through the declared boundary.
levelNotes.L2: Trace synchronous effects and deferred continuations.
levelNotes.L3: Propagate fulfillment and failure through composed or concurrent work.

archetypes.source: ECMAScript and TypeScript language semantics; cores: exercism-javascript, javascript-questions, wtfjs

archetypes.name: Discriminated Union & State Machine Reducer
archetypes.coreConcept: Implementing strict runtime and compile-time state transitions using discriminated union action patterns and type narrowing guards, enforcing exhaustive coverage without unhandled branches.
mentalModel: 1. Define distinct states and event actions characterized by a common discriminant property (e.g. 'type' or 'status').
2. In the transition reducer, narrow action payload types based on the discriminant.
3. Reject invalid state-to-state transitions with descriptive domain errors, guaranteeing state consistency.
archetypes.governingInvariant: newState = transition(currentState, action); invalid transitions throw InvalidStateTransitionError

cognitiveTraps.name: State Mutation on Invalid Transition
cognitiveTraps.description: Permitting transition actions from incompatible states (e.g. CANCELLED -> SHIPPED) corrupts domain state integrity.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Dispatch PAY event on an already REFUNDED order; status changes to COMPLETED.

cognitiveTraps.name: Type Model Erases Useful Distinctions
cognitiveTraps.description: A broad or inaccurate declared type can hide invalid operations or reject valid input shapes.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Strict compiler fixtures assign representative valid and invalid values; broad declarations allow an invalid operation or a narrow declaration rejects a supported state.

realWorldDomains.description: Managing e-commerce payment checkout flow (INITIAL -> AUTHORIZED -> CAPTURED / VOIDED).
Enforcing device firmware update lifecycle (IDLE -> DOWNLOADING -> VERIFYING -> FLASHING).

qualityChecks.check: State transitions return a new state object instead of mutating the current state in place.
qualityChecks.why: Mutating the current state object breaks reducer predictability and corrupts prior snapshots.

qualityChecks.check: Switch or branch chains over a discriminated union include a `default` branch that throws on unknown discriminants.
qualityChecks.why: A missing `default` branch lets newly added action types fall through silently.

qualityChecks.check: State transitions are defined in one place (a transition table or single reducer) rather than scattered across ad-hoc conditionals.
qualityChecks.why: Scattered transition logic makes illegal state edges easy to miss when adding new actions.

levelNotes.L1: Represent primitive and structured values with fitting types.
levelNotes.L2: Keep callback input and result types aligned across transformations.
levelNotes.L3: Use strict compilation alongside behavioral examples to validate the baseline contract.

archetypes.source: ECMAScript and TypeScript language semantics; cores: exercism-typescript, typescript-exercises

archetypes.name: Diagnostic Debugging & Minimal Reproducer Isolation
archetypes.coreConcept: Locating and remediating subtle logical bugs and boundary defects in existing code guided by reproducer test suites without causing regressions.
mentalModel: 1. Run test suite to observe exact assertion failure and reproducer input.
2. Trace variable state changes step-by-step through the defective execution path.
3. Apply targeted remediation preserving external function signature and existing behavior.
archetypes.governingInvariant: failing reproducer test turns Green; all existing baseline tests remain Green

cognitiveTraps.name: Special-Case Patching Instead of Root-Cause Fix
cognitiveTraps.description: Adding an ad-hoc if statement for the specific test case rather than fixing the underlying logical equation.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Add 'if (x === 42) return true;' passing test 1 but failing boundary test with x = 43.

cognitiveTraps.name: Breaking Exported Function Signature
cognitiveTraps.description: Changing the exported function name, parameter order, or return shape breaks existing baseline callers.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Add a required second parameter without a default; baseline single-arg callers throw or fail.

cognitiveTraps.name: Runtime Example Mistaken for Type Safety
cognitiveTraps.description: A value can pass a few runtime examples while violating the intended static contract, or a broad type can erase useful distinctions.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: The behavior examples pass but strict compilation rejects a callback result or permits an invalid operation; separate compiler and runtime checks expose the mismatch.

cognitiveTraps.name: Configured Restriction Assumed to Cover Equivalent Forms
cognitiveTraps.description: A static rule can miss an equivalent access form or reject unrelated behavior when its scope is misunderstood.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Lint fixtures include allowed and prohibited access forms; a missing diagnostic or an extra diagnostic reveals the configuration boundary.

realWorldDomains.description: Fixing URL query string serializer for repeated keys and special character encoding.
Fixing deep object path getter ('a.b.c') when encountering null or intermediate primitives.

qualityChecks.check: The fix addresses the underlying condition or invariant rather than hardcoding an `if` branch for a specific test input.
qualityChecks.why: Special-casing a single reproducer input leaves the root bug intact for all other boundary values.

qualityChecks.check: The fix is localized to the defective logic without unrelated rewrites or leftover workaround branches.
qualityChecks.why: Broad unrequested rewrites in a bugfix introduce new regressions and obscure the root cause.

qualityChecks.check: Compiler feedback and runtime examples are maintained as separate verification concerns with a clear boundary.
qualityChecks.why: Combining both concerns in one opaque check makes failures harder to isolate.

knownBad.code: type View = any; function inspect(view: View) { return view.total.toUpperCase(); }

levelNotes.L1: Use a failing behavioral example to isolate a focused defect.
levelNotes.L2: Check both runtime outcomes and static contracts; test positive and negative rule cases.
levelNotes.L3: Keep the repair tied to the underlying contract and verify regression behavior.

archetypes.source: ECMAScript and TypeScript language semantics; cores: eslint, exercism-javascript, typescript-exercises

archetypes.name: Function Parameters: Defaults, Rest Arguments & Numeric Rounding
archetypes.coreConcept: A function signature controls how missing and variable-length arguments arrive: default parameters apply only when an argument is undefined, rest parameters collect any number of trailing arguments into an array, and money values must be rounded explicitly.
mentalModel: 1. Decide which parameters are required, which have defaults, and which are variadic.
2. Use a default parameter (rate = 0.1) instead of `rate || 0.1`, so an explicit 0 is respected.
3. Collect variadic inputs with a rest parameter (...items) and reduce them with an explicit initial value.
4. Round the final number once, at the end, to the required decimal places and return a number, not a string.
archetypes.governingInvariant: f(a) === f(a, defaultValue) && f(a, 0) applies 0; restArgs.reduce(sum, 0) === 0 when no arguments are passed

cognitiveTraps.name: Falsy Argument Replaced by Default
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `arg || default` replaces a deliberate 0 with the default value.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: applyDiscount(50, 0) returns 45 instead of 50.

cognitiveTraps.name: Reduce Without Initial Value
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling reduce on an empty rest array without an initial value throws a TypeError.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: sumInvoiceTotal(0.07) throws instead of returning 0.

cognitiveTraps.name: toFixed Returns a String
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning `value.toFixed(2)` yields a string, so strict equality with a number fails.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: applyDiscount(19.99) === 17.99 is false because the result is '17.99'.

realWorldDomains.description: Applying optional promotional rates at checkout.
Summing a variable number of invoice lines with tax.

qualityChecks.check: Optional defaults and variadic inputs are expressed cleanly in the function signature or explicit nullish guards rather than mutating `arguments` or using falsy `||` fallbacks.
qualityChecks.why: Falsy `||` fallbacks drop explicit `0` or `false` arguments, and `arguments` obscures the function's contract.

qualityChecks.check: Numeric rounding is applied once at the output boundary as a numeric value, keeping intermediate calculations unrounded.
qualityChecks.why: Rounding intermediate steps accumulates drift, and returning a string from `toFixed` breaks numeric callers.

archetypes.name: Array & Object Basics: Aggregation, Filtering, Nested Access & Immutable Updates
archetypes.coreConcept: Arrays and objects are reference values: read nested fields deliberately, derive new collections with map/filter/reduce, and return new objects or arrays instead of mutating the caller's data.
mentalModel: 1. Identify the input shape (array of numbers, array of objects, nested object, or key-value map).
2. Derive results with non-mutating operations (filter, map, reduce, spread) rather than sort/splice/assignment on the input.
3. For key-value maps, read missing keys with a fallback (?? 0) and write into a copy ({ ...obj, [key]: value }).
4. Format output exactly as specified, including singular/plural wording and rounding.
archetypes.governingInvariant: deepEqual(inputBefore, inputAfter) && output satisfies the specified shape

cognitiveTraps.name: Mutating the Caller's Data
cognitiveTraps.description: Sorting the input array or assigning into the input object changes data the caller still uses.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: adjustStock(stock, 'SKU-1', 2) also changes stock['SKU-1'] in the caller.

cognitiveTraps.name: Missing Key Produces NaN
cognitiveTraps.description: Adding a delta to an undefined map entry yields NaN instead of starting from 0.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: adjustStock({}, 'SKU-9', 3) returns { 'SKU-9': NaN }.

cognitiveTraps.name: Output Not Normalized
cognitiveTraps.description: Forgetting to round, trim or lowercase derived values, or to switch to the singular form.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: buildShippingLabel with one item returns '(1 items)'.

realWorldDomains.description: Summarizing sensor readings without altering the raw series.
Exporting normalized emails of active subscribers.
Formatting labels from nested order data.
Applying stock adjustments immutably.

qualityChecks.check: Updating a key-value map returns a new object rather than mutating the caller's object in place.
qualityChecks.why: Mutating the caller's object causes silent side effects for any other code holding a reference to it.

qualityChecks.check: Data filtering and aggregation are separated from string formatting so derived values remain reusable and testable.
qualityChecks.why: Mixing aggregation with label formatting couples business math to presentation text.

archetypes.name: Runtime Value and Completion Trace
archetypes.coreConcept: A prediction follows the language rules for value category, conversion context, identity, and deferred completion at each observation point.
mentalModel: 1. Mark the value and operation at each expression.
2. Separate immediate effects from deferred continuations.
3. Track what each later observer actually receives.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Each predicted observation matches the value, phase, and completion state available at that point.

cognitiveTraps.name: One Conversion Rule Assumed Everywhere
cognitiveTraps.description: Boolean tests, arithmetic, equality, and runtime classification can apply different rules.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A trace includes the same unusual value in two operator contexts; a predicted output that repeats one conversion result is incorrect.

cognitiveTraps.name: Deferred Reaction Placed in the Synchronous Phase
cognitiveTraps.description: A queued promise reaction cannot interrupt the synchronous sequence already running.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: An exact output prediction places a deferred callback before the remaining immediate statements.

cognitiveTraps.name: Content Mistaken for Identity
cognitiveTraps.description: Equal-looking structured values can still be distinct references.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: A comparison prediction treats two separately created records as identical because their visible fields match.

realWorldDomains.description: Predicting observable behavior in short utility and service traces.

levelNotes.L1: Classify values and predict direct expression results.
levelNotes.L2: Trace identity, coercion context, and synchronous versus deferred observations.
levelNotes.L3: Reason about nested completion and failure propagation; full event-loop depth belongs to PRG-T01-C01-U07.

archetypes.source: ECMAScript and TypeScript language semantics; cores: exercism-javascript, javascript-questions, wtfjs

qualityChecks.check: Every predicted value is tied to the correct expression and execution phase.
qualityChecks.why: A trace can contain individually plausible values in an impossible sequence.

knownBad.code: events.push("start"); Promise.resolve().then(() => events.push("later")); events.push("finish");

qualityChecks.check: Trace material distinguishes immediate observations from deferred continuation points so the reasoning path is inspectable.
qualityChecks.why: A trace without explicit observation boundaries is difficult to review and can conceal an ordering assumption.

knownBad.code: function run() { scheduleLater(); return readNow(); }

archetypes.name: Behavior-Preserving Utility Refactor
archetypes.coreConcept: A local readability refactor preserves the values observed, defaults applied, mutation behavior, and collection contract.
mentalModel: 1. Record the current observable contract, including missing and boundary inputs.
2. Make one local structural change.
3. Compare outputs and side effects across the same cases.
archetypes.governingInvariant: The revised implementation preserves all specified observable behavior while making repeated access or transformation clearer.

cognitiveTraps.name: Readability Change Alters the Contract
cognitiveTraps.description: A refactor can change which property is read, when a default applies, or whether input data is mutated.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Before/after tests include a missing field, a supplied empty-like value, and an unchanged-input assertion; any changed outcome reveals drift.

realWorldDomains.description: Improving readability in small baseline utility functions while preserving behavior.

levelNotes.L1: Refactor repeated property access without changing observed values.
levelNotes.L2: Preserve defaults, nested access behavior, and input mutation boundaries.
levelNotes.L3: Broad architectural refactors belong to later units; keep this chapter diagnostic.

archetypes.source: ECMAScript and TypeScript language semantics; cores: eslint

qualityChecks.check: The change isolates one readability concern and keeps responsibilities and data ownership easy to compare during review.
qualityChecks.why: Unrelated rewrites obscure the intent and make regressions harder to localize.

knownBad.code: function view(record) { return normalize(record).filter(isVisible).map(toSummary).sort(compareSummary); }

qualityChecks.check: The refactor avoids adding a new abstraction unless it clarifies a repeated responsibility within this small baseline utility.
qualityChecks.why: Premature abstraction increases the diagnostic surface without improving ownership.

knownBad.code: class GenericPropertyAccessFacade { read(value, key) { return value[key]; } }

archetypes.name: Behavior and Type Baseline Checkpoint
archetypes.coreConcept: A compact diagnostic implementation must satisfy representative behavior checks and a precise TypeScript contract.
mentalModel: 1. Read the input and output contract.
2. Implement the smallest coherent behavior.
3. run behavior examples and strict type feedback independently.
archetypes.governingInvariant: The implementation satisfies the declared runtime examples and compiles under the stated type constraints.

cognitiveTraps.name: Runtime Example Mistaken for Type Safety
cognitiveTraps.description: A few successful outputs do not establish a sound static type contract.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Runtime examples pass while strict compilation flags a widened or incompatible result type.

realWorldDomains.description: A small implementation checkpoint that combines behavior examples and static checking.

levelNotes.L1: Implement a small behavior from an explicit contract.
levelNotes.L2: Resolve a mismatch found by examples or compiler feedback.
levelNotes.L3: Large validation schemas, advanced type machinery, and project architecture belong to PRG-T01-C02.

archetypes.source: ECMAScript and TypeScript language semantics; cores: exercism-typescript

qualityChecks.check: Behavior examples and compiler feedback are organized as independent evidence sources with failures attributable to each layer.
qualityChecks.why: When verification layers are conflated, a failure cannot identify whether the runtime or declared contract needs attention.

knownBad.code: type Entry = any; function project(entry: Entry) { return entry.label.trim(); }

qualityChecks.check: The checkpoint uses one focused entry point and keeps the diagnostic implementation small enough to explain.
qualityChecks.why: A broad multi-module solution obscures whether the baseline concepts are understood.

knownBad.code: function process(input) { return validate(input).then(normalize).then(persist).then(render); }
